page0.text:
It's past 7 AM.
It's later than usual, but I should make it on time without having to hurry.

page1.text:
It's 7:40 AM.
I go through the gate with plenty of time and as I make my way to the building...
...
I'm overcome with a strange feeling and stop in place.

page2.text: "...What is that? I guess there's nothing wrong..."

page3.text:
It's not like someone is watching me nor is the view any different.
If anything... It would be that it's muted.
Like there's some sort of illusion going on. Everything...the students, the trees, even the school buildings all feel like they've lost their color.

page4.text:
"...Maybe it's my imagination. I might be hypersensitive from everything going on."
I close my eyes and rotate my shoulders.
...But...
Even after taking a deep breath, that unknown strange feeling doesn't disappear.

page5.text:
I go up to the third floor and head to my classroom.
Then...
I run into Tohsaka.

page6.text:
"Yo."
Since we do know each other now, I casually greet her.
"..."
But, Tohsaka is frozen as if she saw a ghost.

page7.text:
"Tohsaka? What, is there something on my face?"
I wipe my cheek with the sleeve of my uniform.
"..."
Tohsaka still doesn't reply.
She looks away and goes back to her classroom.

page8.text:
I'm confused.
What was with that reaction?
I don't think it's like her to ignore someone who greeted her.

page9.text:
...
The strange feeling hits me again once I enter the classroom.
Someone might've brought in some snacks here, since I smell something slightly sweet.

page10.text:
"...I guess the classroom is the same as usual."
I greet the other boys and sit at my seat.
There's ten more minutes until homeroom starts.
I look around the classroom and notice a seat without a bag.

page11.text:
"Shinji's absent, huh?"
Come to think of it, he missed yesterday's practice too.
Despite how he looks, Shinji is punctual and tries hard to follow the rules.
It bothers me a bit that a guy like that has been absent for two days.

page12.text:
The day ends without incident.
Classes are over, and there are only a few students left in the classroom.

page13.text:
...
There's nothing in particular for me to do.
I have to get home before dark as I promised Saber, but...

page14.text:
"...It's not just my imagination. Something has been off since this morning."
Focusing, I take a good look around at my surroundings.
...The strange feeling sticks onto my back.
Perhaps it's because my Magic Circuit can be more easily opened now that I am a Master, but the circuit in my spine senses a subtle chill.

page15.text:
"...I still have time. I'll look around the school for a bit and go home if nothing's wrong..."
I'm a little uneasy at going about this without Saber, but I don't have an easy way to bring her here.
It shouldn't be too dangerous for me to casually look around.

page16.text:
The sun sets.
I looked around school trying not to look suspicious, but I didn't find anything that seemed unusual.

page17.text:
"...I guess it's no use by myself. I'll come and search again with Saber at night."
I grab my bag and leave the classroom.

page18.text:
The sky is tinted crimson.
The sun is setting and it should get dark in an hour or so.

page19.text:
I get to the stairs on the third floor.
As I sling my bag and start to make my way back home, I hear a sound above my head.

page20.text:
"Hm?"
I look up.
There...
Tohsaka is standing firmly at the top of the stairs leading to the fourth floor.

page21.text:
"Oh, you're still here, Tohsaka?"
"..."
She doesn't answer.
First this morning and now this... I feel like her stink eye gets worse every time I see her.

page22.text:
"Hm? What? If you have nothing to say, then I'm going."
I raise my bag to show her I'm going home now.

page23.text:
"...Khh."
What now?
The sigh Tohsaka gives is telling me she's had it up to here.

page24.text:
"I'm stunned. Coming to school without your Servant... Are you insane?"
She mutters in a voice without emotion.

page25.text: "Of course not. Saber can't go into spirit form, so there's no way I can bring her to school."

page26.text:
"Then you should skip school. A Master walking around without their Servant is like asking for others to kill you.
...Emiya, do you know how stupid you are?"

page27.text:
"Wha—I'm not stupid!
Knock it off. Masters don't fight in places where others can see, right? Then during the day, especially at school, is out of the question."

page28.text:
"...All right. Then, let me ask you. Is this a place where others can see?"
"Huh...?"
What is she saying? I don't need to check to see if others can see—

page29.text:
"Huh...?"
How did this...?
Conveniently, there's no one around.
There's no one in the third floor hallway. I'm sure it's also the same for the fourth and the second floor.

page30.text:
The school building, bathed in the setting sun, is completely still.
At this rate, there must only be students or teachers on the first floor...

page31.text:
"It seems like you finally understand.
...Seriously, this morning, I was more pissed than astonished.
I told you so many times, but you still came to get killed."
With a harsh tone of voice, Tohsaka rolls up her left arm's sleeve.
What is...?
A pale and slender arm.
On that feminine arm...
Something like a glowing tattoo appears.

page32.text:
"...The he—"
It's not a Command Spell.
Could that be... I don't have one, but is that a Magic Crest? The proof of a real mage family?

page33.text:
"...I don't need to explain to you, right?
This is the crystallization of the magecraft passed down by my family. I can activate any magecraft carved on here just by passing magical energy through it."
...Right.
A Magic Crest is like an attached engine, separate from the Magic Circuit in a mage.
There is no complicated incantation or procedure to follow.
It is an ultimate shortcut mechanism that makes the car called magecraft run just by turning it on.
But consequently, the Magic Crest won't show up unless it is in use.
A Magic Crest is like another Magic Circuit that is formed when the owner passes magical energy through it.
"I had Archer leave. The Gandr Shot in this crest is enough for you."
Her voice is flat, almost mechanical.
...
That makes me realize that she's serious.

page34.text:
"You can run away, but you'll just be making it hard on yourself. I'm going to win anyway."
She says, coldly.
But my mind is all over the place.

page35.text:
We're going to seriously fight here...?
Why here?
Why now?
Most importantly of all, why does it have to be against Tohsaka...?

page36.text: "H-hold on, Tohsaka! Are you out of your mind? We're at school! Who knows who'll come if we cause a commotion—"

page37.text:
"We'll cross that bridge when we come to it. I have a principle that I won't let the chances in front of me slip by. Sorry, but the coup de grâce comes here.
...And besides, I don't think I can stand having you walk about so carelessly like today."

page38.text:
"I-I said hold on...! I don't have any intention of fighting you—"
"Well I do...! Just prepare yourself, Shirou...!"

page39.text: Tohsaka makes a declaration of war and moves her arm.

page40.text:
"Hrrk...!"
Just what kind of magecraft is that?
The instant Tohsaka points her left arm towards me, my vision is filled with light.

page41.text:
"Ugh...!"
It's about four steps if I leap towards the stairs leading to the second floor.
There's no time to be flustered. I should...
